about.text: Cheese ripened with the help of insects or mites: the larvae of the cheese fly, Piophila casei, that work through Sardinia's sheep's-milk casu marzu, or the mites that colonise the rinds of France's Mimolette and Germany's Milbenkäse during ripening, which help give them their rind and character.

links.name: Journal of Dairy Science (2010), Melnyk et al.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: The mites and larvae are not added to make the curd: they colonise the rind or paste while the cheese ripens. Mites eat the rind, which darkens from yellow to almost black over a year. Fly larvae tunnel inside, and the cheese they leave behind turns very soft.

processing.text: Mites and larvae are not added to make the curd: they colonise the rind or paste while the cheese ripens. Milbenkäse: mites with rye flour, 1–12 mo; casu marzu: larvae, about 3 mo.
